clips.send: A habitat is where an organism lives, like its address. clips.send: Food, water, space, shelter, disease, predators, and weather can all limit population growth. Carrying capacity (K) is the largest population a habitat can support over time under a given set of conditions. Change one condition and see how the curve changes. More rabbits can give foxes enough food to survive and raise more young, so fox numbers may rise after a delay. More hunting can then reduce rabbit numbers, and fox numbers may fall as prey gets scarce. This feedback illustrates ecosystem self-regulation. The model treats rabbits as the foxes’ only prey. Depending on the settings, the curves can rise and fall repeatedly or level off. Drought can also change the pattern.

clips.send: Common mix-up: All the rabbits of one species living in the same meadow at the same time form a population. All the populations in the meadow form a community. The community and the nonliving environment it interacts with form an ecosystem.

clips.send: There are many populations here, including different species of grasses, insects, and fungi, plus rabbits and foxes. All the populations together form a community.

clips.send: Ecological factors (生态因素, shēngtài yīnsù) affect how and where organisms live. Sunlight, water, and temperature are abiotic factors. The grass rabbits eat, the foxes that hunt them, and the microbes that make them sick are biotic factors for rabbits. An ecosystem includes living and nonliving parts. Grasses are producers, rabbits and foxes are consumers, and some bacteria and fungi are decomposers. They interact with water, air, and nonliving parts of the soil.

clips.send: 食物、水、活动空间、隐蔽场所、疾病、天敌和天气都可能限制种群增长。环境容纳量，K，是在一定条件下，环境能长期维持的最大种群数量。改变一个条件，看看曲线怎样变化。 兔子增多后，狐狸的食物更充足，狐群可能过一段时间才增大。捕食增多可能使兔群变小，狐狸又可能因猎物减少而变少。这种相互影响体现了生态系统的自动调节能力。模型假设狐狸只吃兔子。在不同设置下，两条曲线可能反复起伏，也可能逐渐趋于平稳。干旱也可能改变曲线的走势。

clips.send: 环境中影响生物生活和分布的因素叫作生态因素。阳光、水分和温度是非生物因素。兔子吃的草、捕食兔子的狐狸和使兔子患病的病原体，都是影响兔子生活的生物因素。 生态系统由生物部分和非生物部分组成。草是生产者，兔子和狐狸是消费者，有些细菌和真菌是分解者。它们还与水、空气和土壤中的非生物成分相互作用。
